About the Program

The Human Frontier Collective (HFC) brings researchers and scientists together to tackle consequential problems in AI. In partnership with the Preparedness and Policy research team, we are building a small cohort of researchers to work on the empirical foundations of AI safety.

The work includes thinking about various failure modes, evaluating whether safety controls hold up under pressure in realistic settings, and studying how AI agents (mis-)behave over long-horizon tasks. Residents take open research questions like these and turn them into work that improves how frontier AI systems are evaluated and safeguarded.

Mentors will guide AI safety residents on projects in AI safety research areas, such as:

  • AI control and chain-of-thought monitoring: Developing techniques to oversee and constrain AI systems, including monitoring their reasoning to detect harmful intent or deception.

  • Multi-agent safety: Studying the risks that emerge when multiple agents interact, such as collusion, coordinated failures, or unexpected collective behavior.

Scale is looking for a Technical Revenue Accounting Manager to join our growing accounting team in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You will ensure revenue is recorded accurately and on time, support the monthly close, and review contracts both during negotiation and after signature. You will also work on new accounting standards and complex transactions, with room to keep building your technical skills.

The ideal candidate is a detail-oriented, self-motivated team player with strong U.S. GAAP and ASC 606 expertise, a passion for delivering quality results, and a track record of turning technical research into practical solutions.

You will:

  • Own revenue recognition: Ensure revenue is booked correctly and on time, and that the company remains compliant with ASC 606
  • Contract review: Review standard and non-standard contracts, during negotiation and after signature, to determine the appropriate revenue recognition under U.S. GAAP
  • Month-end close: Assist with monthly close activities, including journal entry preparation and review and key account reconciliations
  • Technical accounting: Analyze and operationalize complex transactions under U.S. GAAP including revenue, cost to fulfill, and commissions

jobs.title: US Policy and International Engagement Lead
jobs.description_text:
At Scale, we believe that AI will dramatically improve the world, and our mission is to accelerate the development of AI. As Scale continues to grow its Government Relations and Policy Insights function, we are looking for a US Policy and International Engagement lead to support our engagement with the US government and US-based diplomatic community.

The successful candidate will have experience engaging US Executive Branch and foreign officials, a history of driving policy and regulatory outcomes, and the ability to connect business objectives to policy wins. 

You will: 

  • Develop and execute Scale's US Executive Branch strategy, in close coordination with business units and other cross-functional partners.
  • Engage Executive Branch agencies on Scale’s behalf to forge relationships and advocate for Scale’s policy priorities.
  • Track and advise on US Executive Branch policy and regulatory developments that could impact Scale’s business.
  • Support Scale’s responses to federal rulemakings and requests for comment.
  • Foster Scale’s relationships with the US-based diplomatic community.
  • Support visits by foreign government delegations to Scale’s US offices.
  • Partner with Scale’s Public Sector and Global Public Sector business units to facilitate market entry and expansion in priority markets via diplomatic engagement.

We’re pioneering a new approach to game creation—one in which AI enables creators to work across traditional discipline boundaries, take greater ownership of ideas from concept through launch, and bring more great games to players.

As a Producer, you’ll create the structure, workflows, and momentum that allow a small, AI-native team to move quickly from idea to live game. Business and technical teams use Sigma to explore live data, build intelligent applications, and automate critical workflows, all without moving data or breaking governance. How you'll make an impact

As a member of our Financial Institutions business unit, you will serve as a trusted advisor to bank executives and boards of directors, helping clients navigate complex balance sheet, asset/liability management (ALM), interest rate risk, liquidity, and strategic planning decisions.

You will work closely with CEOs, CFOs, treasury leaders, risk officers, executive management teams, and boards of directors to translate complex financial and balance sheet dynamics into meaningful business insights and actionable strategies. Through thoughtful analysis, effective communication, and deep banking expertise, you will help clients better understand risks, opportunities, and potential outcomes while supporting critical strategic decisions.

Success in this role requires a unique combination of technical expertise, strategic thinking, executive presence, and relationship management. The ideal candidate is equally comfortable analyzing model assumptions and presenting insights in a boardroom, helping decision-makers understand not only what the numbers indicate, but also what actions may be appropriate in response.

In this role, you will:

  • Advise bank management teams and boards of directors on balance sheet strategy, asset/liability management, liquidity, and interest rate risk management.
  • Lead client discussions that connect financial performance, risk exposures, and strategic objectives.

About the Role:

We are looking for a Senior Director, Program Management to serve as the operating backbone of the global Marketing organization. Reporting directly to the CMO, you will build and steward the operating model through which marketing programs and go-to-market efforts are planned, resourced, funded, sequenced, and delivered — across every marketing function and every international market we operate in.

This is not a role that manages a single portfolio. You will partner closely with growth, communications, marketing  (B2B+Brand) and regional teams, and be accountable for the connective tissue between them: the planning process, the marketing budget, the resourcing model, and the systems and tooling the org runs on. You will give the marketing leadership team a full overview “what are we shipping, what will it cost, who is doing it, and when will it land, as well as where a decision, dependency, or trade-off requires leadership attention.”

You will also be expected to lead with AI. We are not looking for someone to rebuild the program management function that existed five years ago — we want a leader who redesigns it around what AI now makes possible.

This is a hybrid role based out of our San Francisco or Los Angeles office. You must be willing to travel to our office two days/week.
